title: Change-log rows for permission-group saves and program access changes are written but hidden from every reader, so Change history and the new Weekly summary never show who changed access in a Flight Program.
steps: 1. Sign in as a Flight Program administrator (group 'Program managers'). 2. Administration > Users: change an observer's groups to 'Program managers' (programUsers:updateAccess). 3. Administration > Permission groups: create a group 'Night crew' with Flight Program administrator (admin:saveGroup). 4. Open Change history and its Weekly summary tab for a period covering today. 5. Repeat step 4 as a system administrator in that program, and again in 'Unassigned records'.
expected: docs/change-history.md: Weekly summary lists 'Users and access' counts and notable 'permission changes (groups saved or deleted, memberships and program access changed)'. The rows user.program_access_changed and group.saved (also user.created, user.program_access_added, group.deleted) appear for the program administrator and the system administrator.
actual: The audit table holds the rows (programUuid = the program, entityUuid = the user id or group id, no aircraft), but auditHistory:page, auditHistory:summary and the snapshot's audit list return none of them to anyone: families.access is 0 and notable has no permission change. A system administrator cannot see them in the program or in Unassigned records either. Only untagged rows (admin:updateUser's user.permissions_changed) show, and only in Unassigned records.
evidence: notes/acl-probe2.json (rows vs managerSummary/rootSummaryInProgram/rootPageUnassigned); src/domain/programs.ts:422-443 buildAuditFilter: a program-tagged row is visible only if entities.has(entityUuid) or its aircraft is visible, and collectVisibleEntities (programs.ts:446-463) holds no user or group ids. convex/auditSummary.test.ts:86-97 hides this by inserting every fixture row with entityUuid = the program uuid.
repro: repro/acl/zz-hunt-acl-1-access-audit-hidden.test.ts (with repro/acl/zzHuntAclWorld.ts; cp both to convex/, npx vitest run convex/zz-hunt-acl-1-access-audit-hidden.test.ts)
suspect: src/domain/programs.ts:434-441 (program-tagged rows) and :446 collectVisibleEntities; convex/auditHistory.ts:147 visibility
notes: Affected writers: convex/admin.ts:377 group.saved (programUuid: args.programUuid), convex/defaultGroups.ts:44, convex/groupDeletion.ts, convex/programUsers.ts user.created / user.program_access_changed / user.program_access_added. A program administrator can promote anyone in the program to program administrator and nobody can see that in the app. Decide who may read these rows (program administrators of that program and system administrators seems intended by the summary's 'access' family) and pin it with a test that uses real mutations, not hand-made rows.

title: An expiring date's change-log rows appear in the snapshot's recent list but never in paged Change history, the record's own history ("History not found.") or the Weekly summary.
steps: 1. As a Flight Program administrator save an expiring date (Settings > Expiring dates; expiringItems:save). 2. Call operations:snapshot: audit holds expiring-date.saved. 3. Call auditHistory:page for the program, auditHistory:page with entityUuid = the item's uuid, and auditHistory:summary for today.
expected: The same visibility rules in all four reads (docs/change-history.md: 'The server builds the summary from the same entries the change log pages, under the same visibility rules'): the row is paged, the item's history opens, the summary counts it.
actual: auditHistory:page omits the row, the entity filter throws ConvexError 'History not found.', and summary.total excludes it. Once more than 250 newer rows exist the row is unreachable in the app.
evidence: notes/acl-probe1.json (managerSnapshotAuditHasExpiring true, managerPageActions without it, managerEntityPage refused). convex/auditHistory.ts:147-181 visibility() loads management, partsRequests, purchaseOrders, checklists, templates and setups but not expiringItems (nor costs), so collectVisibleEntities (src/domain/programs.ts:446) lacks the item uuid; convex/operations.ts:336 loads them for the snapshot.
repro: repro/acl/zz-hunt-acl-2-expiring-history.test.ts (with zzHuntAclWorld.ts; cp both to convex/, npx vitest run convex/zz-hunt-acl-2-expiring-history.test.ts)
notes: Cost rows are also missing from visibility(); check whether cost change-log rows without an aircraft tag (program settings, budgets) have the same gap. System-wide expiring dates (no program) are visible to a system administrator in Unassigned records through the untagged-row rule.

title: A user whose only groups are an aircraft-owner group and a board group gets the full read workspace for the whole fleet (flights, change log, job cards, manuals, attachment URLs, member names), more than either read-only reduced view allows.
steps: 1. In a Flight Program, put one user in 'Aircraft owners' (covering one aircraft) and in 'Board (read-only)' (an aircraft owner who sits on the board). 2. Sign in as that user and load the app (operations:snapshot). 3. Call auditHistory:page for the program.
expected: No more than the union of the owner portal and the board view: no flights, no change log, no other people, no job cards, manuals or attachment URLs; auditHistory:page refused as it is for an owner ('Aircraft owner access is read-only.') and for a board member ('Board access is read-only.').
actual: isOwnerView and isBoardView are both false (each needs every read group to be of its kind), so scopedSnapshot returns the ordinary workspace: all 4 aircraft (the board group covers the fleet), 4 flights, the change log, 8 member names, 4 work orders with tasks, 4 job cards, 4 manuals, 4 work-order attachments with URLs, full problem-report text; checkContext lets every read query through (auditHistory:page returns rows).
evidence: notes/acl-probe1.json key bothView and bothAuditPage; src/domain/ownerView.ts:46-49, src/domain/boardView.ts:79-82, src/domain/programs.ts:286-287, convex/programContext.ts:88-90.
repro: repro/acl/zz-hunt-acl-3-owner-plus-board.test.ts (with zzHuntAclWorld.ts; cp both to convex/, npx vitest run convex/zz-hunt-acl-3-owner-plus-board.test.ts)
notes: docs/board-view.md says 'A user who also holds another kind of group in the program keeps the full workspace, as mixed owner memberships do', which was written for owner + pilot or mechanic. For two reduced-view groups the rule widens access instead of keeping it. Writes stay refused (the groups hold only read). Owner decision: which reduced view (or union) an owner on the board should get; the validation in admin:saveGroup only stops one GROUP carrying both flags, not one USER holding both groups.

title: The owner portal's file whitelist, documented as current Form 337 copies, also sends aircraft owners every logbook page photo of flights and work orders, with download URLs and the linked record ids.
steps: 1. A pilot attaches a logbook line photo to a flight on aircraft 1 and a mechanic attaches a signed-page photo to a work order (aircraftFiles:upload, category logbook-page). 2. Sign in as an aircraft owner of aircraft 1 and load operations:snapshot.
expected: aircraftFiles holds only current Form 337 copies (ownerSnapshot's contract: 'completed work-order summaries and current Form 337 copies'; the owner view holds no flights and no work-order detail).
actual: aircraftFiles holds both photos with category logbook-page, linkedKind, linkedUuid (the flight's and the work order's uuid), file name and a storage URL. A photo of a logbook line shows the pilot's name and signature; a signed work-order page shows the mechanic, certificate number and the work text the owner view otherwise clears.
evidence: notes/acl-probe1.json key ownerFiles; src/domain/ownerView.ts:94-98 filters only by aircraft and isCurrentAircraftFile, written before the logbook-page category existed; convex/operations.ts:122-124.
repro: repro/acl/zz-hunt-acl-4-owner-logbook-photos.test.ts (with zzHuntAclWorld.ts; cp both to convex/, npx vitest run convex/zz-hunt-acl-4-owner-logbook-photos.test.ts)
notes: docs/logbook-photos.md says 'Everyone who reads the aircraft sees the thumbnails', docs/aircraft-photos.md says owners see the Form 337 list; the two disagree once owners count as readers. The owner portal UI may not render the photos, but the data and URLs reach the browser and the 7-day offline snapshot. Board members receive no files (checked).

title: The board whitelist, documented as passing no free text, sends board members AD source notes, AD compliance method, service bulletin and terminating-action text, AD action descriptions and the MEL item text; the owner whitelist sends mechanic names, certificate numbers and user ids it is documented to clear.
steps: 1. On an aircraft, record an AD with source notes (the setup wizard writes 'Method: ...' and the notes column there), a required action with a description, and a compliance entry with method, service bulletin and terminated-by text. 2. Defer an open discrepancy under the MEL with an item text. 3. Load operations:snapshot as a board member and as an aircraft owner.
expected: docs/board-view.md: 'no free text (discrepancy descriptions, notes, reasons, placards, mechanic names and evidence references are cleared)'; src/domain/boardView.ts header: 'Free text, people, rates and files never pass'. ownerSnapshot: 'Internal notes, people and shop detail are cleared'.
actual: Board snapshot contains airworthiness[].source.sourceNotes, tasks[].description, history[].method, history[].serviceBulletin, history[].terminatedBy, discrepancies[].deferral.melItem, plus inspection and component-requirement descriptions. Owner snapshot additionally contains AD history mechanic, certificate, evidence, recordedBy (user id), correctionReason, AD reason, deferral placard, deferredBy (user id) and deferredByName, and inspections' calendarExemptReason and calendarExemptChangedBy (user id).
evidence: notes/acl-probe3.json keys board and owner (MARK- strings that survive); src/domain/boardView.ts:205-241 (toBoardDiscrepancy spreads the deferral, toBoardInspection and toBoardAD are omit-lists, not whitelists), src/domain/ownerView.ts:82-91.
repro: repro/acl/zz-hunt-acl-5-board-free-text.test.ts (with zzHuntAclWorld.ts; cp both to convex/, npx vitest run convex/zz-hunt-acl-5-board-free-text.test.ts)
suspect: src/domain/boardView.ts:228 toBoardAD (spreads r and each history entry) and :205 toBoardDiscrepancy
notes: Inspection reference/description and the AD subject are the names the due list shows, so they probably must pass; the docs should then say so. The fields that look unintended are sourceNotes, method, serviceBulletin, terminatedBy, task descriptions and melItem. convex/tenantIsolation.test.ts and boardView.test.ts only check rateCents/laborRateCents and a few named fields, so the 'no free text' promise has no test. Owner side is lower priority (owners are entitled to their aircraft's compliance records) but the docstring is wrong.

title: Editing a saved shipping address overwrites it in place and writes an address.saved change-log row with no before or after, which no user can read ("History not found.").
steps: 1. As a Flight Program administrator save a new address 'Depot' at 1 Main St (savedAddresses:save). 2. Edit it to 99 Other Rd. 3. Inspect the audit table and open the address's history (auditHistory:page with entityUuid).
expected: CONTEXT/brief: every record change writes an audit row with actor, entity, program and before/after; convex/savedAddresses.ts header: 'every save is audited'. The second row shows 1 Main St before and 99 Other Rd after, and a program administrator can read it.
actual: Both rows hold only actor, program, action and entityUuid: before and after are undefined, the stored row is replaced (ctx.db.replace), so the earlier ship-to address is unrecoverable from the app. The rows are also invisible to everyone (same cause as AC-1: the address uuid is not a visible entity).
evidence: notes/acl-probe3.json keys addressAudit and addressHistory; convex/savedAddresses.ts:82-92.
repro: repro/acl/zz-hunt-acl-6-address-audit.test.ts (with zzHuntAclWorld.ts; cp both to convex/, npx vitest run convex/zz-hunt-acl-6-address-audit.test.ts)
notes: Requests and purchase orders keep their own copy of the address, so issued documents are not rewritten; the gap is the directory entry future orders ship to. Addresses hold a contact name, email and phone, so decide how much of them belongs in the permanent change log.

title: docs/saved-addresses.md says any signed-in member of the program can save addresses, but the server lets only Flight Program administrators save one, so a mechanic's 'Add new address' on a parts request is refused.
steps: 1. Sign in as a maintenance technician (read, discrepancy, resolve, maintenance). 2. Call savedAddresses:save for the active program with a new, complete address (the 'Add new address' window of a parts request).
expected: docs/saved-addresses.md line 3: 'Signed-in members of that program can view and save them'.
actual: ConvexError 'Flight Program administrator required.' for observers, pilots and technicians (src/domain/savedAddresses.ts:108). Only program and system administrators can save.
notes: Either the doc or the rule is wrong. Reading stays open to every program member, including saved contacts' name, email and phone (only inventory LOCATION contacts are blanked for non-administrators in savedAddresses:list).

title: The Weekly summary's refused sign-ins count is always 0 for a Flight Program administrator: real user.sign_in_refused rows carry no program, so the summary's visibility rule hides them.
steps: 1. A Google or Microsoft sign-in is refused for a member (identities:recordRefusal writes user.sign_in_refused, actor 'system', entity the user id, no programUuid). 2. A Flight Program administrator opens Change history > Weekly summary for that day.
expected: docs/change-history.md: 'Refused sign-ins are counted only' in the summary and its CSV row.
actual: summary.refusedSignIns is 0. The row is visible only to a system administrator working in 'Unassigned records' (untagged-row rule), who is not who the summary is written for.
evidence: convex/identities.ts:215-228 (no programUuid), src/domain/programs.ts:441-442; convex/auditSummary.test.ts:86-97 and :113-118 insert the fixture's refusal row with programUuid and entityUuid = the program, which real rows never have.
repro: repro/acl/zz-hunt-acl-8-refused-signins.test.ts (with zzHuntAclWorld.ts; cp both to convex/, npx vitest run convex/zz-hunt-acl-8-refused-signins.test.ts)
notes: Same root as AC-1: the summary's fixtures do not match the rows the app writes. A refusal is deployment-wide (the stranger may belong to no program; see known A10), so the owner should decide whether program administrators see a count at all or only system administrators do.

title: An aircraft transfer leaves the aircraft's expiring dates (registration, insurance) in the source program: the new program never sees or is alerted about them, and the source program keeps the alert but can no longer edit the item.
steps: 1. In program A, as program administrator, save an expiring date 'N-number registration' linked to aircraft 3 (expiringItems:save with aircraftUuid). 2. As system administrator transfer aircraft 3 to program B (programs:transfer). 3. Load the snapshot as B's program administrator and as A's. 4. As A's administrator change the item's date.
expected: The expiring date follows its aircraft (or the transfer refuses or warns): B's administrators see and get alerts for the registration expiry of the aircraft they now operate; A holds no item for an aircraft it no longer has.
actual: B's snapshot has expiringItems []; A's still lists the item with aircraftUuid sample-aircraft-3 and keeps its alert. A's edit is refused with 'Aircraft must belong to this Flight Program.' (it can only archive it, or drop the aircraft link). B cannot take the item over ('Record belongs to another Flight Program.') and must retype it.
evidence: notes/acl-probe4-transfer.json (sourceExpiring, destExpiring, sourceEdit, destTakesOver); convex/programs.ts:110-135 loadTransfer loads management, inspections, checklists and component setups only; src/domain/expiringItems.ts:292-294.
repro: repro/acl/zz-hunt-acl-9-transfer-expiring.test.ts (with zzHuntAclWorld.ts; cp both to convex/, npx vitest run convex/zz-hunt-acl-9-transfer-expiring.test.ts)
suspect: convex/programs.ts:110 (loadTransfer) and src/domain/programTransfers.ts (expiring dates not among the records an aircraft carries)
notes: Also seen after the transfer, lower priority: A's purchase orders keep lines pointing at the moved aircraft, its inspection and its work order (SAMPLE-PO-3; an issued order cannot be closed until received); A's groups keep the aircraft id (documented). Logbook page photos, Form 337 copies, manuals, job cards and their change-log rows follow the aircraft correctly, and A can no longer read them. docs/flight-program-access.md lists what a transfer carries and does not mention expiring dates.

title: An aircraft transfer hands the destination program the source program's cost records for the aircraft (labor lines with the source's hourly rate and mechanic names, other costs, the budget), counts the source's spending in the destination board's totals, and removes them from the source program's own cost history.
steps: 1. In program A set a labor rate, add labor (2 h at $95) and a $450 hangar fee to a work order on aircraft 3, and set its 2026 budget (costs:execute). 2. As system administrator transfer aircraft 3 to program B. 3. Load the snapshot as B's program administrator, a B technician and a B board member, and as A's administrator.
expected: Docs list what an aircraft transfer carries (flights, discrepancies, inspections, components); cost records are 'administrator data' of the program that spent the money. Either they stay with A's books, or the transfer says it moves them and re-tags them.
actual: B's administrator receives the work-order cost record with rateCents 9500, technician 'Source Mechanic', 'Source hangar fee' 45000 and the budget, all still tagged programUuid = A; B's technician gets the labor line (name and minutes); B's board view shows quarterCents and yearCents 64000 against A's budget for money B never spent. A's snapshot has no cost record for the aircraft any more, so A's spend for the period is gone from its reports, and A's budget.set is refused ('Aircraft not found.'). The rows keep A's tag until B edits them (the budget is re-tagged on B's next save; the work-order record is not).
evidence: notes/acl-probe7-transfer-costs.json (costRows, destAdminCosts, destTechCosts, destBoardCosts, sourceCostsForMoved, costRowsAfter); convex/programContext.ts:284-304 costDocs reads by aircraft, src/domain/programs.ts:379-396 scopeCost checks only the aircraft.
suspect: convex/programContext.ts:289 and src/domain/programs.ts:387 (cost records scoped by aircraft, not by their program)
notes: Only a system administrator can transfer, so this needs no attacker; it is what a legitimate sale or loan of an aircraft between programs does today. Owner decision: do cost records follow the aircraft (then say so in docs/flight-program-access.md and re-tag them) or stay with the program that paid.

title: Addendum to AC-3 and AC-5: complete list of the fields the board view and the owner portal pass, and of what an owner-plus-board user gets beyond both.
steps: 1. cp repro/acl/zz-hunt-acl-fields.test.ts src/domain/ 2. HUNT_OUT=<dir> npx vitest run src/domain/zz-hunt-acl-fields.test.ts 3. Read <dir>/acl-reduced-view-fields.json, or notes/acl-reduced-view-fields.md.
expected: A test that pins the whitelist field by field, as docs/board-view.md promises ('the tenant-isolation suite ... checks the whitelist').
actual: No test pins it. Board, free text or people still passing: airworthiness[].source.sourceNotes, .sourceHistory[].source.sourceNotes, .tasks[].description, .history[].method, .history[].serviceBulletin, .history[].terminatedBy; discrepancies[].deferral.melItem; management[].description and management[].manualReference.{manualUuid,section,printedPage,pdfPage} (removed from inspections but not from components and requirements); inspections[].description, .reference, .sourceKey; workOrders[].scope (documented). Owner, in addition: airworthiness[].reason, .history[].{mechanic,certificate,evidence,recordedBy,correctionReason}; discrepancies[].description, .deferral.{placard,deferredBy,deferredByName}; inspections[].calendarExemptReason, .calendarExemptChangedBy, .manualReference.*. Both: the active program's address, contact name, email and website; the full aircraft row; own member record.
repro: repro/acl/zz-hunt-acl-fields.test.ts (three cases: the list, the board free-text pin, the owner-plus-board pin; the last two fail today)
notes: The filler adds every zod schema key, so a field added to a schema later shows up in the list without touching the test. boardSnapshot passes aircraft[].photoUrl when the snapshot already holds one (the server adds none for the board; check the demo adapter).

title: pushSubscriptions:subscribe accepts any https URL as a device's push endpoint, so every member with read access can make the server POST to a host of their choice whenever an urgent alert fires.
steps: 1. As an observer (read only) call pushSubscriptions:subscribe with endpoint 'https://push.example.test/b-device' (not a push service) and well-formed keys. 2. When the VAPID variables are set and the program has an urgent alert, urgentAlerts:sendImmediate hands the member's devices to push:sendUrgent.
expected: Only known push services are accepted (fcm.googleapis.com, updates.push.services.mozilla.com, *.push.apple.com, *.notify.windows.com), as most Web Push servers enforce, or the choice is recorded as accepted risk.
actual: The subscription is stored (src/domain/pushSubscription.ts:31-36 checks only length, URL syntax and the https prefix). convex/push.ts:119-126 then fetches that URL with a signed VAPID Authorization header and the encrypted payload, up to 10 endpoints per member, on every new urgent alert.
evidence: notes/acl-matrix-compact.txt (pushSubscriptions:subscribe allowed for observer, pilot, tech, manager with a non-push host); src/domain/pushSubscription.ts:31-36; convex/push.ts:108-140.
notes: The storing is proven; the outbound request was read in code, not run (no external calls allowed, VAPID unset). Impact is limited: requests leave Convex's cloud (no private network), redirects are refused, the JWT audience is the attacker's own origin, and the payload is encrypted to keys the caller supplied. It gives a member a server-side request trigger and a way to burn the action's 15 s timeout per device. Related: a member who becomes board-only or owner-only keeps their device rows and cannot call unsubscribe ('Board access is read-only.').
